global_layoffs.description: Meta eliminated about 8,000 positions and canceled 6,000 planned hires while reorganizing around major artificial-intelligence infrastructure spending and shifting staff toward AI-related roles.
Canva cut 1,271 employees, or about 22% of its workforce, while flattening its organization and citing changing technology and product expectations.
SUSE announced a workforce reduction of approximately 10%, with its chief executive stating that automation and AI are fundamentally changing how software companies operate.
NICE cut about 500 jobs while changing how it organizes and invests to serve customers deploying AI-driven contact-center technology.
Fiserv disclosed that 3,000 employee and contractor positions had been eliminated since June and linked continued simplification to an AI-everywhere operating model.
Block announced a second 2026 workforce reduction and said improved tools would allow employees to handle more routine work, without disclosing a job count.
PayPal said it was pursuing approximately $700 million in run-rate savings through cuts affecting more than 2,000 jobs while adopting AI tools including customer-service chat agents.
Amazon cut about 250 jobs in its devices and services unit as it sought to operate more efficiently and align staffing with its product roadmap.

saudi_policy_updates.title: Phased increase of the Nitaqat full-worker salary threshold to SAR 5,000 then SAR 6,000
saudi_policy_updates.description: The minimum monthly salary for a Saudi employee to count as one full worker toward Saudization rates rises from SAR 4,000 to SAR 5,000 on 2027-04-25 and to SAR 6,000 on 2028-04-25; HRDF Employment Support aligns its minimum supported wage on the same two steps. It is a counting threshold, not a general minimum wage.
saudi_policy_updates.source: Saudi Press Agency via Saudi Gazette; EY Tax News (https://taxnews.ey.com/news/2026-2304-saudi-arabia-raises-minimum-nitaqat-salary-threshold-for-saudi-employees)

ai_workforce_signals.headline: Meta shifts workforce toward AI infrastructure
ai_workforce_signals.description: Meta eliminated about 8,000 positions, canceled 6,000 planned hires, and increased its focus on AI infrastructure. The restructuring is also moving thousands of employees into AI-related roles while reducing staffing elsewhere.

ai_workforce_signals.headline: AI-linked technology layoffs exceed 90,000 in 2026
ai_workforce_signals.description: Layoffs.fyi data cited in November reporting attributed more than 93,000 technology-sector job cuts to AI during 2026. The broader tracker recorded more than 135,000 technology layoffs across 334 companies by late October.

ai_workforce_signals.headline: Enterprise AI adoption reshapes software staffing
ai_workforce_signals.description: SUSE said automation and AI are fundamentally changing software-company operations as it announced a workforce reduction of approximately 10%. The development illustrates pressure on software firms to redirect headcount toward AI capabilities and higher-value roles.

ai_workforce_signals.headline: AI contact-center deployment drives operating redesign
ai_workforce_signals.description: NICE cut about 500 jobs while reorganizing investment around enterprise customers deploying AI contact-center systems. The shift signals continued consolidation of traditional customer-service work around AI-agent platforms.

ai_workforce_signals.headline: Financial-services firms pair cost reduction with AI adoption
ai_workforce_signals.description: PayPal linked more than 2,000 job cuts and cost savings to operational simplification while adopting AI customer-service agents. Fiserv separately connected thousands of reductions to an AI-everywhere operating model.

ai_workforce_signals.headline: Canva restructures amid generative-technology pressure
ai_workforce_signals.description: Canva eliminated 1,271 roles, about 22% of its workforce, while flattening its organization. Its leadership cited technology-driven changes in what users create and expect, although it did not explicitly identify AI as the cause of the reductions.

ai_workforce_signals.headline: AI remains mixed with broader restructuring motives
ai_workforce_signals.description: Analysis of 2026 layoff announcements found that many companies mentioning AI also cited cost control, organizational simplification, changing strategy, or slower growth. The evidence supports treating AI as a contributing factor in many cases rather than assuming direct substitution.

weekly_stats.notable_trend: AI-related restructuring is increasingly combining headcount reductions with redeployment toward infrastructure, software automation, and customer-service agents, while companies continue to present AI alongside broader efficiency and organizational simplification goals.
